review_notes:
I read the whole file. I also grepped the repo for downstream uses of `coderiv`, `coderivEquivTaylor` and `taylorComponent`. Those uses are in TaylorComponent.lean, GradedCoderivation.lean, Induced.lean and BarDifferential.lean. I did not open any of them in full. The simp-tagged lemmas are `isCoderivation_coderiv`, `letter_comp_coderiv`, `mem_coderivations`, `coderivEquivTaylor_apply`, `coderivEquivTaylor_symm_apply`, and the `taylorComponent_*` lemmas (`_apply`, `_zero`, `_coderiv`, `_add`, `_smul`).

I found no justified problem with any of them. Their left-hand sides are distinct and every right-hand side is simpler than its left-hand side, so I see no credible cycle and no competing rule. `taylorComponent_coderiv` matches the function-position subterm `taylorComponent (coderiv R F) n` before `taylorComponent_apply` can unfold it, so the two do not clash. Lemmas that need side conditions (`coderivSummand_eq_zero`, `coderivSummand_tprod`, `coderiv_subword`, the `letter_splice_*` lemmas) are correctly left unannotated. A bare simp lemma for `coderiv_subword` would be unsuitable because `K` is a free variable.

I considered adding linearity lemmas for `coderiv` in `F` (zero, add, smul). A grep of the repo found no uses of `coderiv_add`, `coderiv_zero` or `coderiv_smul`, so I did not report this. I have not run Lean, so nothing here comes from observed simplifier behaviour.
